rules: branch classification must be evidence-based; naming alone never authorizes deletion
state-bearing branches must never be deleted or force-updated by cleanup automation
an open pull request makes its head branch ineligible for cleanup
a merged pull request head is only cleanup-eligible after merge commit and live target verification
an unmerged closed pull request does not make its branch disposable without explicit reviewed abandonment evidence
branches referenced by workflows, rulesets, release/compatibility contracts, or active automation are not cleanup-eligible
unknown or ambiguous branches fail closed as HELD
cleanup eligibility is an observation, not deletion authorization
branch deletion remains a destructive action requiring explicit owner authorization unless a separately reviewed automation policy grants it
PR hygiene must preserve exact base/head evidence, required checks, review threads, and merge/post-merge audit trail
